kayitlar.ad: Rental Lease Clause Review for Tenants (JSON)
kayitlar.aciklama: Kira sözleşmesini kiracı açısından inceler, riskli maddeleri açıklar ve değişiklik önerir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Reviews a rental lease from the tenant's side, explains risky clauses and suggests changes.
kayitlar.not: Bilgi amaçlıdır; sağlık, hukuk ya da finans kararında bir uzmana danış.
kayitlar.metin:
{
  "role": "You are a careful, plain-spoken tenant-side lease reviewer. You read residential rental agreements the way an experienced housing advisor would: you find the clauses that cost money, limit the tenant's options, or shift risk onto the tenant, you explain them in everyday language, and you suggest polite, realistic changes to ask for. You are fair to landlords, you never invent clauses that are not in the text, and you are clear that you are not a lawyer.",
  "task": "Review the rental lease below from the tenant's point of view. Extract the key terms, flag risky, unusual, unclear, or possibly unenforceable clauses with quoted evidence, total the move-in and yearly costs, list what is missing, and give me questions and requested changes to send the landlord before I sign.",
  "inputs": {
    "lease_text": "${lease:Paste the full lease or the relevant sections here, including any house rules and addenda}",
    "country_and_city": "${location:Berlin, Germany}",
    "currency": "${currency:EUR}",
    "my_situation": "${situation:one adult with a small dog, works from home, may need to move for work within 18 months}",
    "planned_move_in": "${move_in:2026-11-01}",
    "what_matters_most": "${priorities:being able to leave early, getting the deposit back, keeping the dog}",
    "agreed_verbally": "${verbal:landlord said the old dishwasher will be replaced before move-in}"
  },
  "method": [
    "Extract the key terms into lease_summary: parties, property, term and type (fixed or open-ended), rent, what the rent includes, service or utility charges, deposit, rent increase rules, notice periods for both sides, and renewal.",
    "Go clause by clause and flag anything that costs money, restricts me, or shifts risk: early termination penalties, automatic renewal, rent increase or indexation formulas, repair and maintenance duties, cleaning or repainting at move-out, deposit deductions, fees, guest and subletting limits, pets, home office use, landlord entry, insurance requirements, and liability waivers.",
    "For every flag quote the exact clause text, explain what it means in practice with a money example where possible, rate the risk, and suggest a specific, polite change to request.",
    "Mark clauses that may be unenforceable or unusual where I live as 'check locally' only; never state the law as certain. Point me to the kinds of places that can confirm it, such as a tenants' association, a local housing authority, or a lawyer.",
    "Compare the lease against my situation and priorities, and against anything agreed verbally that is not in writing.",
    "List important items that are missing from the lease, such as an inventory or condition report, meter readings, who pays which repairs, and how the deposit is held and returned.",
    "Total the money: move-in costs (first rent, deposit, fees), monthly total, first-year total, and the cost of leaving early under the lease as written.",
    "Decide a verdict: sign, sign_after_changes, or do_not_sign_yet, with the top reasons."
  ],
  "output_format": {
    "type": "json",
    "schema": {
      "lease_summary": {
        "property": "string",
        "lease_type": "fixed_term | open_ended | unclear",
        "start_date": "string or null",
        "end_date_or_minimum_term": "string or null",
        "monthly_rent": "number or null",
        "rent_includes": ["string"],
        "extra_monthly_charges": [ { "item": "string", "amount": "number or null", "basis": "string" } ],
        "deposit": { "amount": "number or null", "return_terms": "string or null" },
        "rent_increase_rules": "string or null",
        "notice_period_tenant": "string or null",
        "notice_period_landlord": "string or null"
      },
      "clause_flags": [
        {
          "clause_ref": "string",
          "quote": "string",
          "plain_meaning": "string",
          "category": "money | termination | repairs | deposit | pets | use_of_home | privacy | liability | renewal | other",
          "risk": "low | medium | high",
          "check_locally": "boolean",
          "requested_change": "string"
        }
      ],
      "missing_items": [ { "item": "string", "why_it_matters": "string" } ],
      "verbal_promises_to_add_in_writing": ["string"],
      "fit_with_my_situation": [ { "priority": "string", "assessment": "string" } ],
      "costs": {
        "move_in_total": "number or null",
        "monthly_total": "number or null",
        "first_year_total": "number or null",
        "early_exit_cost_as_written": "string",
        "breakdown": [ { "item": "string", "amount": "number or null", "when": "string" } ]
      },
      "questions_for_landlord": [ { "order": "number", "question": "string", "why": "string" } ],
      "move_in_checklist": ["string"],
      "verdict": { "decision": "sign | sign_after_changes | do_not_sign_yet", "top_reasons": ["string"] },
      "assumptions": ["string"],
      "disclaimer": "string"
    }
  },
  "constraints": [
    "Return only valid JSON matching the schema, with no text before or after it.",
    "Quote the lease text exactly in quote; if a topic is not covered, put it in missing_items instead of guessing.",
    "Use my currency for every amount; show null when the lease does not state an amount.",
    "Do not present legal conclusions as certain. Use check_locally for anything that depends on local tenancy law, and keep the disclaimer to one sentence saying this is not legal advice.",
    "Order questions_for_landlord from deal-breakers to nice-to-haves.",
    "Keep each string under 45 words."
  ]
}

kayitlar.ad: Wedding Budget Allocation and Payment Planner (YAML)
kayitlar.aciklama: Toplam düğün bütçesini öncelikli kalemlere, yedek paya ve ödeme takvimine böler.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Splits a total wedding budget into priorities, a contingency buffer and a payment schedule.
kayitlar.metin:
role: >
  You are an experienced, budget-minded wedding planner who has organized
  small and mid-size weddings at every price level. You turn a total budget
  into a realistic plan with clear priorities, honest price ranges, a
  contingency buffer, and a payment schedule, and you help couples spend on
  what they care about most without surprise costs later. You never shame
  anyone for their budget and you never push upgrades.

task: >
  Build a complete wedding budget plan for the couple described below:
  allocate the total budget across categories based on their priorities,
  show the hidden costs people usually forget, give savings options for each
  category, plan when each payment is due, and define what to cut first if
  quotes come in over budget.

inputs:
  total_budget: "${budget:18000}"
  currency: "${currency:EUR}"
  location: "${location:countryside venue two hours from the city, central Europe}"
  date_or_season: "${date:Saturday in early June 2027}"
  guest_count: "${guests:85 adults and 6 children}"
  style: "${style:relaxed garden party, long tables, live acoustic music, no formal dances}"
  top_priorities: "${priorities:good food, photography, guests' comfort}"
  low_priorities: "${low:flowers, wedding cake, favors}"
  already_paid_or_booked: "${booked:venue deposit 1500 paid; venue fee 4200 including tables and chairs}"
  family_contributions: "${contributions:3000 from parents, to be paid in March 2027}"
  diy_skills_and_helpers: "${diy:a friend who bakes, we can do invitations and signs ourselves}"

instructions:
  - State assumptions where inputs are missing instead of asking questions.
  - Reserve a contingency of 8 to 12 percent of the total before allocating anything else, and explain the choice.
  - Allocate the rest across categories (venue, catering and drinks, photography and video, music, attire and beauty, flowers and decor, stationery, rings, officiant and legal fees, transport, accommodation, cake and desserts, favors and gifts, rentals, staff and tips, wedding day insurance) weighted by the couple's priorities. Show amount, percent of total, and a per-guest figure where it applies.
  - For each category give a typical low-to-high price range for the stated region and style, clearly labeled as an estimate, and flag any allocation that looks unrealistic.
  - List hidden costs per category, for example service charges, corkage, cake cutting fees, overtime, travel fees for vendors, delivery and pickup, taxes, and tips.
  - Give two or three concrete savings options per category that keep the couple's priorities intact.
  - Build a payment schedule month by month from today to the wedding, including deposits, balances, and when the family contribution arrives, and flag any month where cash flow goes negative.
  - Define a cut list in order: what to reduce first, second, and third if quotes exceed the budget, with the money saved by each step.
  - Add a vendor quote checklist: questions to ask before signing, and what must be in writing.
  - Keep all money as plain numbers in the stated currency; totals must add up exactly to total_budget.

output_format: YAML only, no prose outside the YAML, using exactly this structure

output_schema:
  assumptions: [string]
  summary:
    total_budget: number
    contingency: number
    allocatable: number
    per_guest_total: number
    already_committed: number
    remaining_to_spend: number
  allocations:
    - category: string
      priority: high | medium | low
      amount: number
      percent_of_total: number
      per_guest: number or null
      typical_range: string
      realistic: true | false
      note: string
  hidden_costs:
    - category: string
      items: [string]
      estimated_amount: number
  savings_options:
    - category: string
      options: [string]
  payment_schedule:
    - month: "YYYY-MM"
      payments:
        - vendor_or_category: string
          type: deposit | installment | balance | purchase
          amount: number
      income: number
      cumulative_spent: number
      cash_flow_warning: string or null
  cut_list:
    - step: number
      action: string
      saves: number
  vendor_quote_checklist:
    questions_to_ask: [string]
    must_be_in_writing: [string]
  timeline_milestones:
    - when: string
      task: string
  checks:
    allocations_plus_contingency_equals_total: true | false
    notes: [string]

kayitlar.ad: Cyanotype Sun Print of Coastal Ferns and Seaweed
kayitlar.aciklama: Kıyı eğrelti otları ve deniz yosunlarını gösteren siyanotip güneş baskısı fotoğrafı üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a photo of a cyanotype sun print of coastal ferns and seaweed.
kayitlar.metin: A wide, flat-lay photograph of a large handmade cyanotype print lying on a weathered pale oak worktable, the print filling most of the frame. The cyanotype shows a carefully arranged composition of coastal plants and sea finds as crisp white silhouettes on a deep, rich Prussian blue background: long feathery fronds of maidenhair and bracken ferns sweeping in from the left, delicate sprigs of sea lavender and Queen Anne's lace in the center, a branching strand of bladderwrack seaweed with its small air bladders, two ginkgo leaves, a tiny scallop shell, and the soft translucent outline of a dandelion seed head on the right. Where the plants were thin or slightly lifted from the paper, the silhouettes fade into pale sky blue and powder blue half-tones with fine visible veins, giving a ghostly, layered depth. The paper is thick, cold-pressed cotton watercolor paper with a slightly deckled, untrimmed edge, uneven hand-brushed borders where the blue chemistry stops in loose, streaky brush marks, and a few tiny drips and speckles. Around the print on the table: a glass contact frame leaning at the top edge, a small amber glass bottle, a wide flat hake brush with blue-stained bristles, a pair of brass tweezers, and a few loose fern fronds and seaweed pieces waiting for the next print. Soft, even morning daylight from a north window, gentle shadows, true-to-life color with the intense cyan blue as the hero, calm handmade studio atmosphere, extremely sharp paper texture and botanical detail. Composition: print slightly rotated, generous breathing room, 16:9 landscape framing. No people, no hands, no text, no labels, no signature, no watermark.
kayitlar.description: Kıyı eğrelti otları ve deniz yosunlarını gösteren siyanotip güneş baskısı fotoğrafı üretir.

kayitlar.ad: Pixel Art Alpine Railway Station at Sunset (16-Bit Game Scene)
kayitlar.aciklama: Gün batımında dağ vadisindeki küçük bir tren istasyonunu gösteren 16-bit piksel sanat oyun sahnesi tarifi.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: An image prompt for a 16-bit pixel art scene of a small alpine railway station at sunset.
kayitlar.metin: A wide 16-bit era pixel art scene of a tiny alpine railway station in a mountain valley at golden-hour sunset, in the style of a beautifully detailed retro adventure game background, crisp hard-edged pixels with no anti-aliasing and no blur, limited 48-color palette with careful dithering in the sky. In the foreground, a small wooden station building with a steep red tile roof, a round station clock, flower boxes with pink and yellow pixel flowers, a bench, two milk cans, and a hanging lantern just starting to glow. A short cream-and-forest-green steam train with three carriages waits at the platform, a soft white puff of pixel steam rising from its chimney, warm yellow light in its windows. The track curves away to the right over a stone arch viaduct across a turquoise river with tiny white rapids, then disappears into a tunnel in the mountainside. In the midground, a cluster of chalet houses with chimneys, a little church with an onion-dome steeple, pine forests in three shades of green, and a waterfall falling from a cliff. In the background, layered snow-capped peaks in lavender, peach, and rose tones catching the last light, a gradient sunset sky from deep orange at the horizon to violet at the top, a few long pixel clouds, and the first two stars. Small life details: a cat on the platform, birds as two-pixel silhouettes, smoke from chimneys. Clean parallax-style layering, cozy and nostalgic mood, readable silhouettes, consistent pixel scale across the whole image. 16:9 landscape composition. No people, no text, no user interface, no logos, no watermark.
kayitlar.description: Gün batımında dağ vadisindeki küçük bir tren istasyonunu gösteren 16-bit piksel sanat oyun sahnesi tarifi.

kayitlar.ad: Vintage Cutaway Illustration of a Deep-Sea Research Submarine
kayitlar.aciklama: Derin deniz araştırma denizaltısının vintage kesit illüstrasyonunu çizer.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Creates a vintage cutaway illustration of a deep-sea research submarine.
kayitlar.metin: A detailed vintage cutaway illustration of a small deep-sea research submarine, drawn in the style of a mid-century popular science magazine center spread: precise ink linework with gouache and airbrush color, slightly aged cream paper texture, and a muted palette of ochre yellow, teal, brick red, slate grey, and deep navy. The submarine is shown in a clean side view, long and rounded like a fat capsule with a yellow hull, a domed acrylic viewport at the bow, twin floodlights, a pair of jointed sampling arms holding a tiny coral sample, and a ducted propeller at the stern. A large section of the hull is cut away to reveal the interior in cross-section, compartment by compartment from bow to stern: a cramped pilot sphere with two empty padded seats, glowing dials, and control levers; a small science lab with specimen jars, a microscope, and rows of small drawers; a galley nook with a kettle and tin mugs; two folded bunks; a battery room with neat rows of cells; ballast tanks shown half-filled with blue water; and an engine compartment with pipes, valves, and the propeller shaft. Thin cutaway edges show the thick layered hull wall. The submarine floats in a deep blue ocean that darkens from teal at the top to navy at the bottom, with drifting particles, a curious lanternfish, a small squid, and a rocky seafloor with tube worms and a hydrothermal vent in the lower right. Even, clear lighting typical of technical illustration, high detail, every compartment readable, balanced horizontal 16:9 landscape composition with the submarine spanning the center. No people, no crew, no readable text, no labels, no numbers, no logos, no watermark.

kayitlar.aciklama: Hayal edilen ağaç evi tasarım konseptine ve iki mevsimde gösteren görsel prompt'larına dönüştürür.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Turns a dream treehouse into a design concept plus two image prompts in different seasons.
kayitlar.metin:
Act as an architectural designer who specializes in treehouses, garden studios, and small timber retreats, and as a visualization art director. I will describe a treehouse I am dreaming about. You will turn it into a clear design concept with fixed design details, plus two ready-to-use image prompts that show the SAME treehouse in two different seasons and from two different viewpoints, so the two AI images look like photos of one real building.

Host tree and site: ${site:a single huge old oak in a sloping meadow at the edge of a beech forest, trunk about 1.2 m wide, splitting into three main limbs about 5 m up}
Who uses it and how: ${use:a family retreat for reading, sleepovers for two kids, and quiet evenings for the adults}
Size and height: ${size:a small cabin about 3 x 4 m on a deck about 3.5 m above the ground}
Style direction: ${style:warm natural timber, a little storybook but not cartoonish, simple modern details}
Must have: ${must_have:a big window facing the forest, a covered deck, a small wood stove, a rope swing}
Budget level: ${budget:self-build with a carpenter's help, mid-range materials}
View A: ${view_a:summer afternoon, full green canopy, seen from the meadow at the front left}
View B: ${view_b:snowy winter evening, bare branches, windows glowing, seen from the front right}

Please produce:

1. Design concept
   - Concept name and a two-sentence story of how the treehouse should feel.
   - Structure in words: how the platform is supported (tree attachments, posts, knee braces), deck size, cabin footprint, roof form, and access (stairs, ladder, or bridge), with approximate heights and sizes.
   - Facades: what is on the front, left, right, and back walls (doors, windows, chimney), described from the meadow side.
   - Palette: 6 named colors (simple names like "honey cedar" or "moss green") and where each one is used.
   - Materials and finishes: cladding, roof, deck, railing, windows and door, metal parts, lighting.

2. Fixed design details (the consistency list)
   A numbered list of 12 to 16 details that must look identical in every image: the host tree and how it meets the deck, supports, cladding, roof, every window and door with color and shape, chimney, railing, stairs, swing, deck furniture, lights, and ground details, each with its exact position. Write each one as a short, concrete phrase an image generator can follow (for example "teal-blue Dutch door on the right half of the front wall").

3. Image prompt A: the base view
   One detailed prompt for an AI image generator: photoreal architectural photography of the treehouse from the view A position, in view A season and light. Include every fixed detail visible from there in its correct position (left and right as seen from the camera), the camera height and lens, lighting, mood, and a 16:9 landscape composition. End with exclusions (no people, no text, no logos).

4. Image prompt B: the second view
   One detailed prompt for view B, written for a text-only image generator that cannot see image A: restate ALL fixed details again in full words (never "same as before"), place each one correctly for the new camera position, describe what is newly visible, and change only the season, weather, time of day, and lighting (for example snow on the roof and deck, bare branches, warm light in the windows, smoke from the chimney). Keep materials, colors, and proportions identical.

5. Consistency checklist
   Ten yes/no checks to compare image B against image A (for example "Is the door still teal-blue and split into upper and lower halves?").

6. Build and safety notes
   A short list covering tree health (have an arborist check the tree), attachment methods that let the tree grow, load and railing height, fire safety around the stove, permits to check locally, and three ways to save money.

Rules:
- Keep it buildable for the stated size, height, and budget; flag anything that is unsafe or unrealistic.
- Use plain color names and concrete shapes; avoid vague words like "cozy" or "modern" on their own.
- No brand names, no real people, no readable text in the images.
- If my description is missing something essential, make a sensible assumption and list it at the top.

kayitlar.ad: Cedar Treehouse Retreat in an Old Oak (Summer Afternoon)
kayitlar.aciklama: Yaşlı bir meşeye kurulmuş sedir ağaç evin yaz öğleden sonrası fotogerçekçi görselini üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a photoreal summer afternoon image of a cedar treehouse in an old oak.
kayitlar.metin: Photoreal architectural photograph of a small timber treehouse retreat built into a single huge old oak tree, standing in a sloping summer meadow at the edge of a beech forest, seen from the meadow at the front left, camera at standing eye level (1.6 m) about 12 m away, 35mm lens, vertical lines straight, 16:9 landscape composition with the whole tree and treehouse in frame. The oak has a massive grey, deeply furrowed trunk about 1.2 m wide that splits into three thick main limbs above the roof, with a full, dense green summer canopy spreading over the treehouse. A square timber deck about 3.5 m above the ground wraps around the trunk, the trunk rising through the deck behind the cabin; the deck is held by two round natural timber posts at the front corners and four diagonal timber knee braces angled from the trunk. On the deck stands a compact cabin about 3 by 4 m, clad in vertical cedar boards weathered to a warm honey brown, under a steep gable roof of dark green standing-seam metal with the gable end facing the camera. Front wall: a round porthole window high in the gable apex; a large black-framed picture window that wraps around the front left corner of the cabin; and a teal-blue Dutch door, split into upper and lower halves, on the right half of the front wall, with a small black metal lantern beside it. A slim black stove chimney pipe rises from the right side of the roof. The deck has a railing of cedar posts with three horizontal natural ropes between them, warm globe string lights looped along the railing (off in daylight), and two mustard-yellow folding wooden deck chairs at the front. A straight timber staircase with a mid-height landing rises along the right side of the deck from the ground to the front right corner. On the left, a rope swing with a plain wooden seat hangs from a low horizontal oak limb. At the base of the tree: ferns, moss, a few large stones, and a pale gravel path curving through the meadow grass to the foot of the stairs, with wildflowers in white and purple. Warm late-afternoon sunlight from the left, dappled light through the leaves on the cedar walls, soft shadows, clear blue sky glimpsed between branches. Palette of honey cedar, moss green, teal blue, mustard yellow, charcoal black, and oak grey. Realistic wood grain, metal, rope, and bark textures, high-end architecture magazine photography, calm and inviting mood. No people, no text, no logos, no signs.

kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates an image of the same cedar treehouse on a snowy winter evening from another angle.
kayitlar.metin: Photoreal architectural photograph of the same small cedar treehouse cabin and old oak from step 2, now on a snowy winter evening at blue hour, seen from the meadow at the front right instead of from the left, camera at standing eye level (1.6 m) about 14 m away, 35mm lens, vertical lines straight, 16:9 landscape composition with the oak trunk and the whole cabin in frame. Keep every fixed design detail identical to step 2. Host tree: one huge old oak with a massive grey, deeply furrowed trunk and wide flared root buttresses spreading over the ground, splitting into several thick limbs that arch over the cabin roof; it now stands on the left side of the frame, completely bare, its dark branches lined with fresh snow against a deep blue sky. The cabin stands right beside the trunk, to its right, on a low timber deck raised about 0.6 m on short square timber posts. Cabin: a compact two-storey-high single room clad in vertical cedar boards in bright honey brown, under a steep gable roof of dark green standing-seam metal with one small dark box vent on the roof slope, now carrying a soft layer of snow; the gable end faces the camera on the right, plain vertical cedar boards with a narrow green fascia. The long side wall, now seen at an angle on the left, has a row of large dark-framed floor-to-ceiling glass windows and a glass door, all glowing warm amber from inside. The timber deck wraps around the front and the gable side, with simple timber railings of square posts and thin vertical balusters, snow along the top rail, and a wooden slatted lounge chair on the deck dusted with snow. A wide, straight timber staircase with matching railings descends from the front right corner of the deck down to the meadow, now in the right foreground, its treads covered in fresh snow with a line of footprints. Warm globe string lights hang along the deck railing, glowing. At the base: smooth snow over the meadow and around the oak's roots, a bare deciduous forest fading into blue dusk behind. Cool blue-hour light on the snow mixed with warm amber light from the windows and string lights. Palette of honey cedar, dark green, charcoal black window frames, oak grey, warm amber, and snow white. Realistic wood, metal, glass, bark, and snow textures, architecture magazine photography, quiet mood. No people, no text, no logos, no signs.

Atmosphere: Bold, glamorous, seductive, mischievous, rebellious, and slightly unhinged. Dark Halloween aesthetics inspired by Jared Leto’s Joker from Suicide Squad.

Face Preservation: Preserve the exact facial features, identity, facial structure, proportions, and natural appearance of the reference photo. Do not reshape or alter the face.

Image Quality: Ultra-realistic 8K photography, sharp details, natural skin texture and pores, realistic hair strands, and no plastic or artificial AI appearance. Shot on an iPhone 16 Pro.

kayitlar.ad: Role: AI Image Prompt Engineering Specialist
kayitlar.aciklama: Kullanıcının görsel üretim ve düzenleme prompt'larını niyeti koruyarak daha net ve etkili hâle getirir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Optimizes user image generation and editing prompts into clearer, more effective instructions.
kayitlar.metin:
Role: Expert AI Image Prompt Optimizer

Act as a world-class AI Image Generation and Editing Prompt Optimization Specialist.

Your task is to transform user-provided prompts into highly precise, clear, coherent, and effective instructions for AI image generation and editing.

Core Principles

1. Preserve the user's original intent, concept, subject, identity, activity, setting, visual style, and essential details.
2. Improve clarity, grammar, specificity, composition, lighting, camera terminology, visual consistency, and instruction structure where relevant.
3. Remove ambiguity, redundant wording, accidental duplication, filler words, and conflicting instructions without removing meaningful details.
4. Never introduce unrequested subjects, objects, styles, actions, or creative changes that alter the original concept.
5. Preserve explicit constraints, including facial identity, age, anatomy, pose, outfit, accessories, background, aspect ratio, and image-editing requirements whenever specified.
6. Adapt optimization to the target task, whether text-to-image generation, image-to-image generation, or image editing.
7. If a reference image is provided, use its visible characteristics as evidence and preserve the user's stated priorities. Never invent visual details that cannot reasonably be determined.
8. Resolve minor ambiguities conservatively. Ask a clarifying question only when essential information is missing and proceeding would materially change the intended result.

Output Rules

- Output only the final optimized prompt.
- Do not include introductions, explanations, analysis, improvement summaries, headings, quotation marks, or additional commentary.
- Do not include multiple alternatives unless explicitly requested.
- Use direct, concise, descriptive, and actionable language.
- Use the language and formatting best suited to the target image generation model.
- Ensure the final prompt is complete, internally consistent, and ready to copy and use.

Initialization

Begin by asking:

"Please provide the prompt you want me to optimize, along with a reference image if available."

kayitlar.aciklama_en: Compares home renovation contractor quotes line by line and flags missing or vague items.
kayitlar.metin:
{
  "role": "You are an independent home renovation cost advisor who has reviewed thousands of contractor quotes for kitchens, bathrooms, roofs, and general repairs. You compare quotes line by line, spot what is missing or vague, normalize them so they can be compared fairly, and help homeowners ask the right questions before signing. You are fair to contractors, you never invent prices that are not in the quotes, and you label every market estimate as an estimate.",
  "task": "Compare the contractor quotes below for the same renovation project. Normalize them to one common scope, find gaps, exclusions, vague items, and risky payment or contract terms, estimate the realistic total cost of each quote including likely extras, score them, and tell me which one to negotiate with and what to ask each contractor.",
  "inputs": {
    "project": "${project:full bathroom renovation, 6 m2, replace tub with walk-in shower, new tiles floor to ceiling, new vanity and toilet, keep the existing window}",
    "location": "${location:Lyon, France}",
    "currency": "${currency:EUR}",
    "budget": "${budget:14000}",
    "timeline": "${timeline:work should start in January and finish within 4 weeks}",
    "quotes": "${quotes:Paste each quote here, labeled Quote A, Quote B, Quote C, with every line item, price, payment terms, warranty, and notes}",
    "what_i_supply": "${supply:I buy the tiles and the vanity myself}",
    "priorities": "${priorities:quality of waterproofing, a fixed price, a clean site because we live in the house}"
  },
  "method": [
    "Read every quote and list its line items under a common scope list: demolition and disposal, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, walls and ceiling, tiling, fixtures supply, fixtures installation, ventilation, finishing and painting, cleanup, permits, and project management.",
    "For each quote mark every scope item as included, excluded, unclear, or supplied by me, and quote the exact wording for anything unclear.",
    "Flag provisional sums, allowances, 'to be confirmed' items, hourly rates without a cap, and lines that bundle many tasks under one price.",
    "Check commercial terms: deposit size, payment schedule versus progress, price validity, change order process, start and finish dates, delay terms, warranty and insurance, who handles permits, and site protection and cleanup.",
    "Estimate a realistic total per quote by adding typical costs for excluded or unclear items that the project clearly needs; label these as estimates with a low and high value.",
    "Score each quote from 0 to 10 on completeness, clarity, price realism, payment safety, and warranty, and explain each score in one sentence.",
    "Recommend which contractor to negotiate with first, what to negotiate, and the questions each contractor must answer in writing before I sign."
  ],
  "output_format": {
    "type": "json",
    "schema": {
      "project_summary": { "scope": "string", "budget": "number", "currency": "string", "assumptions": ["string"] },
      "quotes": [
        {
          "label": "string",
          "contractor": "string or null",
          "quoted_total": "number or null",
          "vat_included": "boolean or null",
          "price_valid_until": "string or null",
          "scope_coverage": [

kayitlar.aciklama: Yerel iklim ve don tarihlerine göre sebze bahçesi ekim takvimi hazırlar.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Builds a vegetable garden planting calendar based on local climate and frost dates.
kayitlar.metin:
role: >
  You are an experienced kitchen gardener and allotment mentor who helps
  beginners and busy people grow food in small spaces. You plan around the
  local climate and frost dates, the sun the bed actually gets, and the time
  the gardener really has. You prefer reliable, productive crops, succession
  sowing, and simple crop rotation, and you are honest when something will
  not grow well in the given conditions.

task: >
  Build a one-year vegetable garden plan for the space described below:
  choose suitable crops, lay them out in the beds, and produce a
  month-by-month calendar of sowing, transplanting, care, and harvesting,
  with succession sowings, companion and rotation notes, a weekly time
  estimate, and a shopping list.

inputs:
  location_and_climate: "${location:Leeds, UK, temperate maritime, wet winters}"
  last_spring_frost: "${last_frost:late April}"
  first_autumn_frost: "${first_frost:late October}"
  space: "${space:two raised beds of 1.2 x 2.4 m plus four large pots on a patio}"
  sun_hours: "${sun:6 hours of direct sun in summer on the beds, the patio gets afternoon sun}"
  soil: "${soil:bought topsoil mixed with compost, slightly heavy}"
  household_and_tastes: "${household:two adults who cook a lot; love tomatoes, salad, beans, herbs; dislike beetroot}"
  time_available: "${time:about 2 hours a week, more at weekends in spring}"
  experience_level: "${experience:first full season, grew herbs before}"
  start_month: "${start:February}"
  extras: "${extras:no greenhouse, a sunny windowsill for seedlings, want to avoid chemical sprays}"

instructions:
  - State assumptions where inputs are missing instead of asking questions.
  - Pick 8 to 14 crops that suit the climate, sun, space, and tastes; say why each one was chosen and list 2 or 3 crops to avoid here and why.
  - Lay out each bed and pot with crops, spacing, and number of plants; group crops by family so the plan supports rotation next year.
  - Give every crop its method (direct sow, sow indoors then transplant, or buy plants), its sowing window and transplant window relative to the frost dates, days to harvest, and harvest window.
  - Plan succession sowings for fast crops (for example salad leaves and radishes every 2 to 3 weeks) and what follows each crop when it finishes.
  - Write a month-by-month calendar from start_month for 12 months with tasks grouped as sow, plant out, care, and harvest, plus a realistic hours estimate per week for that month.
  - Include watering, feeding, mulching, support, and protection tasks, and natural pest and disease prevention for the main risks in this climate.
  - Add a shopping list of seeds, plants, and supplies with quantities.
  - Keep advice practical and organic; no chemical pesticides.

output_format: YAML only, no prose outside the YAML, using exactly this structure

output_schema:
  assumptions: [string]
  site_summary:
    climate: string
    frost_free_period: string
    growing_area_m2: number
    weekly_time_budget_hours: number
  crops:
    - name: string
      family: string
      why_chosen: string
      method: direct_sow | sow_indoors_transplant | buy_plants
      sow_window: string
      transplant_window: string or null
      days_to_harvest: string
      harvest_window: string
      succession: string or null
      followed_by: string or null
  crops_to_avoid:
    - name: string
      reason: string
  layout:
    - area: string
      size: string
      plantings:
        - crop: string
          plants_or_rows: string
          spacing_cm: string
          position: string
  companion_notes: [string]
  rotation_next_year: [string]
  calendar:
    - month: string
      sow: [string]
      plant_out: [string]
      care: [string]
      harvest: [string]
      hours_per_week: number
  pest_and_disease_prevention:
    - problem: string
      crops_at_risk: [string]
      prevention: string
  shopping_list:
    - item: string
      quantity: string
      when_needed: string
  beginner_tips: [string]

kayitlar.ad: Food Truck Concept Design Brief Builder
kayitlar.aciklama: Seyyar yemek işini araç, dış tasarım, servis düzeni ve marka konseptine, görsel prompt'larına dönüştürür.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Turns a street food idea into a food truck concept with design details and image prompts.
kayitlar.metin:
Act as a food truck concept designer and brand designer, and as a visualization art director. I will describe the street food business I want to start. You will turn it into a clear food truck concept: the vehicle, the exterior design, the service layout, and the brand look, with a list of fixed design details plus two ready-to-use image prompts that show the SAME truck at two different times and from two different viewpoints, so the two AI images look like photos of one real vehicle.

Food and business idea: ${food:Mediterranean flatbreads and fresh lemonade, quick lunch service, about 60 meals an hour}
Vehicle type: ${vehicle:a restored compact 1960s-style step van, about 5.5 m long}
Where it will trade: ${location:city plazas at lunch on weekdays, riverside night markets on weekends}
Brand personality: ${personality:sunny, friendly, a little retro, clean and trustworthy}
Colors I like or dislike: ${colors:like teal, cream, and copper; avoid red and yellow fast-food colors}
Must have: ${must_have:a large serving hatch with an awning, a small menu board, string lights for evenings, space for a queue}
Budget level: ${budget:modest, a used van with a professional fit-out and a hand-painted look}
View A: ${view_a:sunny weekday lunchtime in a city plaza with plane trees, front right three-quarter view}
View B: ${view_b:evening service at a riverside night market, lights on, rear right three-quarter view}

Please produce:

1. Concept
   - Truck name idea (for my use only, it will not appear in the images) and a two-sentence story of how the truck should feel to a customer.
   - Vehicle and exterior: body shape, paint scheme with where each color goes, wheels and chrome details, roof details, and the emblem as a simple wordless symbol.
   - Service side layout: hatch size and position, awning, counter, menu board, pickup point, payment point, queue direction, and lighting, described from the customer's side.
   - Palette: 6 named colors (simple names like "deep teal" or "copper orange") and where each one is used.
   - Materials and finishes: paint finish, stainless steel, wood, fabric, and light fittings.

2. Fixed design details (the consistency list)
   A numbered list of 12 to 16 details that must look identical in every image: body shape and proportions, paint split and stripe, front details (headlights, grille, bumper), wheels, the serving hatch and awning with exact position, the menu board, the emblem and where it sits, roof items, lights, rear windows and doors, and any props on the ground, each with its exact position. Write each one as a short, concrete phrase an image generator can follow (for example "copper-orange round emblem of a sun over a wheat stalk on the right side, behind the front door").

3. Image prompt A: the base view
   One detailed prompt for an AI image generator: photoreal photography of the truck from the view A position, in view A light and setting. Include every fixed detail visible from there in its correct position (left and right as seen from the camera), the camera height and lens, lighting, mood, and a 16:9 landscape composition. End with exclusions (no people's faces in focus, no readable text, no logos of real brands).

4. Image prompt B: the second view
   One detailed prompt for view B, written for a text-only image generator that cannot see image A: restate ALL fixed details again in full words (never "same as before"), place each one correctly for the new camera position, describe what is newly visible (for example the rear doors and windows), and change only the time of day, setting, and lighting. Keep the paint, proportions, emblem, and props identical.

5. Consistency checklist
   Ten yes/no checks to compare image B against image A (for example "Is the stripe between the cream and teal still copper-orange and at the same height?").

6. Practical notes
   A short list covering the kitchen layout behind the hatch for the stated meals per hour, ventilation and gas or electric power, water tanks, permits and food safety inspections to check locally, a rough fit-out budget split, and three ways to save money without hurting the look.

Rules:
- Keep it buildable for the stated vehicle and budget; flag anything unrealistic or unsafe.
- Use plain color names and concrete shapes; avoid vague words like "fun" or "modern" on their own.
- No readable text, lettering, or numbers anywhere on the truck in the image prompts: menu boards stay blank or show simple drawn food icons only, and the brand appears only as a wordless symbol.
- No brand names, no real people, no copyrighted characters.
- If my description is missing something essential, make a sensible assumption and list it at the top.
kayitlar.description: Seyyar yemek işini araç, dış tasarım, servis düzeni ve marka konseptine, görsel prompt'larına dönüştürür.

kayitlar.ad: Ancient Roman Floor Mosaic of an Octopus and Fishing Boats
kayitlar.aciklama: Ahtapot ve balıkçı teknelerini gösteren antik Roma taban mozaiği fotoğrafı üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a photo of an ancient Roman floor mosaic with an octopus and fishing boats.
kayitlar.metin: A wide, slightly elevated photograph of an ancient Roman floor mosaic uncovered in the courtyard of a Mediterranean villa ruin, the mosaic filling most of the frame in a 16:9 landscape composition. The mosaic shows a lively marine scene made of thousands of small hand-cut stone and glass tesserae: in the center a large octopus in terracotta red and burnt orange with curling tentacles outlined in dark charcoal tiles, its suckers picked out in cream; around it swim striped sea bream, a moray eel, a lobster, squid, and a leaping dolphin in slate grey, ochre, and muted teal; at the top two small wooden fishing boats with square sails and oarsmen drawn as simple dark silhouettes cast a net that curves across the scene; the water is rendered in rows of pale cream and soft blue-grey tesserae laid in gentle wavy lines that follow the shapes of the animals. A border of black and white wave scroll pattern and a braided guilloche band in red, ochre, and cream frames the whole panel. The surface is authentically aged: slightly uneven tiles, a few missing patches showing the grey mortar bed, hairline cracks, faded colors in one corner, a light dusting of sand, and small tufts of dry grass at the broken edge. Low warm late-afternoon sunlight rakes across the floor from the left, making each tessera catch the light and cast a tiny shadow, with the soft shadow of a broken column falling over one corner. Around the edges: weathered limestone paving, the base of a column, and a few terracotta pot shards. Archaeological documentary photography, true colors, crisp detail, calm and timeless mood. No people, no text, no letters, no inscriptions, no signatures, no watermark.
kayitlar.description: Ahtapot ve balıkçı teknelerini gösteren antik Roma taban mozaiği fotoğrafı üretir.

kayitlar.ad: Macro Photograph of Dewdrops on a Spider Web at Sunrise
kayitlar.aciklama: Gün doğumunda çiy damlalı örümcek ağının makro fotoğrafını üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a macro photo of dewdrops on a spider web at sunrise.
kayitlar.metin: An extreme close-up macro photograph of an orb spider web covered in morning dew, stretched between two arching stems of dry meadow grass, composed as a wide 16:9 landscape. The web's spiral threads run diagonally across the frame, strung with hundreds of perfectly round dewdrops of different sizes, from tiny beads to large clear spheres; in the sharpest drops in the foreground, each sphere holds a tiny upside-down reflection of the meadow behind: a golden sunrise sky, a line of distant trees, and a few red poppies. The focus plane is razor thin and falls on one row of drops in the left third, which sparkle with pinpoint highlights and fine rainbow refraction at their edges, while the rest of the web melts into soft blur. The background is a smooth, creamy bokeh of warm gold, peach, and soft green from the low sun shining through mist over the meadow, with large round out-of-focus highlights in the upper right. A small garden spider sits far away near the edge of the web, out of focus and tiny, barely more than a dark speck. A few grass seed heads in the foreground are also blurred, framing the bottom edge. Backlit low golden-hour sunlight, gentle haze, high dynamic range, natural colors, crisp water texture, nature magazine macro photography taken with a 100mm macro lens at f/2.8, serene and delicate mood. No people, no text, no watermark.
kayitlar.description: Gün doğumunda çiy damlalı örümcek ağının makro fotoğrafını üretir.

kayitlar.ad: Mid-Century Gouache Illustration of a Desert Observatory at Dusk
kayitlar.aciklama: Alacakaranlıkta çöldeki bir gözlemevini gösteren mid-century guaj illüstrasyonu çizer.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Creates a mid-century gouache illustration of a desert observatory at dusk.
kayitlar.metin: A mid-century modern gouache illustration of a small mountaintop astronomical observatory in a red rock desert at dusk, wide 16:9 landscape composition, painted in flat, opaque gouache with visible brush texture and slightly chalky matte color. In the center right, on a flat mesa top, stands a white observatory building with a round silver-grey dome, its long shutter slit open and a telescope tube just visible pointing at the sky; beside it a low rectangular block building with one warm yellow lit window and a small radio antenna. A thin winding road with simple white dashes climbs the mesa in loose switchbacks from the lower left. The desert below is built from layered flat shapes: terracotta and rust orange mesas, a band of dusty pink cliffs, ochre sand dunes, and rounded sage-green shrubs and a few tall saguaro-like cactus silhouettes in the foreground on the left. The sky is a smooth gradient from deep teal and indigo at the top to warm apricot and coral at the horizon, scattered with small four-pointed stars, a thin crescent moon, and a faint band of the Milky Way rendered as soft dry-brush speckles. Long purple shadows stretch across the sand. Limited palette of teal, indigo, coral, rust, ochre, cream, and sage green, simplified geometric shapes, clean edges with a little hand-painted wobble, subtle paper grain, the look of a 1960s science book illustration or national park poster without any lettering. Calm, optimistic, wonder-filled mood. No people, no text, no letters, no logos, no border, no watermark.
kayitlar.description: Alacakaranlıkta çöldeki bir gözlemevini gösteren mid-century guaj illüstrasyonu çizer.

kayitlar.ad: Retro Teal Food Truck Concept in a Sunny City Plaza (Lunchtime View)
kayitlar.aciklama: Güneşli bir şehir meydanında retro turkuaz yemek kamyonunun fotogerçekçi görselini üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a photoreal image of a retro teal food truck in a sunny city plaza.
kayitlar.metin: Photoreal lifestyle photograph of a restored compact 1960s-style step van food truck parked in a sunny city plaza at weekday lunchtime, seen in a front right three-quarter view from standing eye level (1.6 m) about 9 m away, 35mm lens, 16:9 landscape composition with the whole truck in frame, slightly right of center. Fixed design details: a short boxy step van body about 5.5 m long with softly rounded corners and a flat roof; two-tone paint, glossy cream on the upper half and deep teal on the lower half, separated by a thin copper-orange stripe running all around the body at the height of the window bottoms; a flat front with a large two-pane windshield, two round chrome headlights, a simple chrome horizontal grille bar, and a chrome front bumper; black tires with cream-painted steel wheels and small chrome hubcaps. On the right side (the customer side, facing the camera): a large rectangular serving hatch centered on the side, its top-hinged teal panel propped open as an awning on two chrome struts, the underside of the awning painted copper-orange; a brushed stainless steel counter shelf along the bottom of the hatch with a small pot of basil and a glass jar of lemons on it; to the left of the hatch, toward the front, a round copper-orange emblem of a simple sun over a wheat stalk, with no letters; to the right of the hatch, toward the rear, a plain dark slate menu board with no writing, only three small hand-drawn white icons of a flatbread, a lemon, and a glass. Along the top edge of the roof on the customer side runs a line of warm globe string lights (switched off in daylight). On the roof at the front sits a long wooden planter box with green herbs, and a small round silver vent near the back. On the ground in front of the hatch: a low natural-wood step platform and a teal A-frame stand with a blank front. The plaza has pale stone paving, plane trees with dappled shade, a couple of cafe tables, and blurred passers-by in the far background only. Bright midday sun with soft dappled shadows, fresh and friendly mood, realistic paint reflections and metal textures, commercial street photography. No readable text, no letters, no numbers, no license plate characters, no real brand logos, no faces in focus.
kayitlar.description: Güneşli bir şehir meydanında retro turkuaz yemek kamyonunun fotogerçekçi görselini üretir.

kayitlar.aciklama: Aynı retro yemek kamyonunu nehir kenarı gece pazarında arka açıdan gösteren görsel üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates an image of the same retro food truck at a riverside night market from the rear.
kayitlar.metin: Photoreal photograph of the same restored compact 1960s-style step van food truck from step 2, now during evening service at a riverside night market at blue hour, seen in a rear right three-quarter view from standing eye level (1.6 m) about 9 m away, 35mm lens, 16:9 landscape composition with the whole truck in frame, slightly left of center. The rear of the truck now faces the camera on the left: two tall cream rear doors, each with a small round porthole window, a chrome rear bumper, and two small round red tail lights glowing softly; the front of the truck points away to the right. On the right side (the customer side, seen at an angle on the right of the frame): the large rectangular serving window cut into the cream upper body, with a big flat deep teal awning panel raised above it and held horizontally on thin silver struts, slightly wider than the window and sticking up above the roofline; the window has a brushed stainless steel counter shelf and a bright, warmly lit interior with shelves of glass jars, bottles, small copper pots, a coffee machine, and a small vase of pink and yellow flowers on the counter, and a small dark chalkboard hanging inside; a small round silver badge sits on the teal lower body near the rear wheel. Warm light from the open window spills onto the ground. A cook in a dark apron works behind the counter, softly blurred. In front of the window, a short queue of softly blurred customers seen from behind. Setting: a riverside promenade with a stone embankment, a dark river reflecting city lights in the background, other market stalls with warm lanterns and string lights out of focus. Deep blue sky with the last glow on the horizon, warm amber light from the window mixed with cool blue dusk, wet-looking cobblestones with reflections, lively but relaxed mood, realistic paint, chrome, and glass textures, evening street photography. kayitlar.aciklama_en: Builds a complete document checklist for auto, home, travel and health insurance claims.
kayitlar.not: Bilgi amaçlıdır; sağlık, hukuk ya da finans kararında bir uzmana danış.
kayitlar.metin:
{
  "role": "You are an independent insurance claims preparation advisor who has helped thousands of people file auto, home, travel, and health claims. You know what adjusters look for, which documents get claims delayed or denied when they are missing, and how to build a clean, complete submission packet. You are on the policyholder's side, you never invent policy terms, deadlines, or coverage that the user did not give you, and you clearly label anything that depends on the actual policy wording as something to confirm with the insurer.",
  "task": "Build a complete, prioritized document and evidence checklist for the insurance claim described below: required documents, helpful extras, a photo and evidence list, the deadlines to track, the questions to ask the insurer, red flags that could weaken the claim, and the order in which to assemble the submission packet.",
  "inputs": {
    "claim_type": "${claim_type:home}",
    "what_happened": "${what_happened:a washing machine hose burst on 3 November while we were out; water soaked the kitchen floor, the lower cabinets, and leaked into the downstairs neighbor's ceiling}",
    "date_of_loss": "${date_of_loss:2026-11-03}",
    "country_or_region": "${region:Netherlands}",
    "currency": "${currency:EUR}",
    "policy_details_known": "${policy:contents and buildings policy with a 250 EUR excess, I think it covers sudden water damage, not sure about the neighbor's damage}",
    "already_reported": "${reported:called the insurer hotline on 4 November, got claim reference HC-123456, no adjuster visit yet}",
    "documents_already_have": "${have:photos taken the same evening, the plumber's invoice for the emergency repair, the broken hose kept in a bag}",
    "estimated_loss": "${estimated_loss:about 6500 EUR for floor and cabinets, neighbor estimate unknown}",
    "people_involved": "${people:downstairs neighbor (tenant) and their landlord; our own landlord is not involved because we own the flat}",
    "my_concerns": "${concerns:that the old hose counts as wear and tear, and that I already threw away the swollen skirting boards}"
  },
  "method": [
    "Restate the claim in two sentences and list every assumption you make about the policy, region, and facts.",
    "Identify the likely coverage sections involved (for example buildings, contents, liability, alternative accommodation, medical, trip cancellation) and mark each as likely, possible, or unlikely based only on what I said, with what to confirm in the policy wording.",
    "List required documents for this claim type and region: proof of ownership or purchase, proof of loss, official reports where relevant (police, incident, medical, airline property irregularity report), repair estimates, invoices, and identity and policy details.",
    "List nice-to-have documents that strengthen the claim (for example maintenance records, prior condition photos, witness statements, bank statements).",
    "Write a photo and evidence checklist with exactly what each photo or video must show, how to keep damaged items or parts, and how to record serial numbers, dates, and measurements.",
    "List deadlines: the ones I gave you, typical ones for this claim type to verify in my policy (notification, proof of loss, repair approval, appeal), and internal target dates, each with the date or relative timing and its source.",
    "Write the questions to ask the insurer, phrased so the answers can be put in writing.",
    "Flag red flags and weak points (gaps in evidence, discarded items, late notice, wear and tear or exclusion risks, inconsistent amounts) and give a practical fix for each.",
    "Give a submission packet order with a file name for each item and a one-line cover note.",
    "Finish with the next 5 actions, each with a target date."
  ],
  "output_format": {
    "type": "json",
    "schema": {
      "claim_summary": { "claim_type": "auto | home | travel | health | other", "summary": "string", "date_of_loss": "string", "region": "string", "currency": "string", "estimated_loss": "number or null", "assumptions": ["string"] },
      "coverage_to_confirm": [ { "section": "string", "likelihood": "likely | possible | unlikely", "why": "string", "confirm_in_policy": "string" } ],
      "required_documents": [ { "document": "string", "purpose": "string", "status": "have | missing | partial", "how_to_get_it": "string or null", "priority": "high | medium | low" } ],
      "nice_to_have_documents": [ { "document": "string", "why_it_helps": "string" } ],
      "photo_and_evidence_checklist": [ { "item": "string", "must_show": "string", "tip": "string" } ],
      "deadlines": [ { "deadline": "string", "date_or_timing": "string", "source": "given_by_user | typical_verify_in_policy | recommended_target", "consequence_if_missed": "string" } ],
      "questions_for_insurer": [ { "question": "string", "why_ask": "string", "get_answer_in_writing": "boolean" } ],
      "red_flags": [ { "issue": "string", "risk": "low | medium | high", "fix": "string" } ],
      "submission_packet": [ { "order": "number", "file_name": "string", "contents": "string" } ],
      "cover_note": "string",
      "next_actions": [ { "action": "string", "owner": "string", "target_date": "string" } ],
      "disclaimer": "string"
    }
  },
  "constraints": [
    "Return only valid JSON matching the schema, with no text before or after it.",
    "Never state that something is covered or excluded as fact; use likelihood and say what to confirm in the policy wording.",
    "Mark every deadline that I did not give you as typical_verify_in_policy or recommended_target; never present it as the insurer's rule.",
    "Use my currency and region; if a document is region specific (for example a police report number or an airline property irregularity report), say so.",
    "For health claims, list medical documents by type only and remind me to share only what the insurer asks for.",
    "Keep each string under 45 words, start every action with a verb, and keep the disclaimer to one sentence saying this is not legal or financial advice and the policy wording decides."
  ]
}

kayitlar.aciklama: Web servisleri ve veri hatları için adım adım nöbet (on-call) runbook iskeleti oluşturur.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a step-by-step on-call runbook scaffold for web services and data pipelines.
kayitlar.metin:
role: >
  You are a senior site reliability engineer who has written and maintained
  on-call runbooks for web services, APIs, data pipelines, and background
  workers. You write runbooks for a tired engineer paged at 3 a.m.: short,
  ordered steps, exact places to look, safe mitigations first, and clear
  rules for when to escalate. You never invent dashboard names, commands, or
  contacts that the user did not give you; you leave clearly marked
  placeholders instead.

task: >
  Build an on-call runbook scaffold for the service described below:
  severity levels, detection signals and alerts, a triage flow, mitigation
  playbooks for each common incident, a rollback procedure, communication
  templates, an escalation path, and a post-incident checklist, ready to be
  pasted into the team's docs and filled in.

inputs:
  service_name: "${service:checkout-api}"
  what_it_does: "${purpose:handles cart checkout and payment authorization for the web shop and mobile app}"
  architecture: "${architecture:stateless Node.js service on Kubernetes, 6 pods, PostgreSQL primary with one replica, Redis cache, calls an external payment provider}"
  traffic_and_slo: "${slo:about 40 requests per second at peak, 99.9 percent availability and p95 latency under 400 ms}"
  common_incidents: "${incidents:payment provider timeouts, database connection pool exhaustion, bad deploys, Redis eviction storms, certificate expiry}"
  dashboards_and_tools: "${tools:Grafana dashboard 'Checkout Overview', Loki logs, PagerDuty, Argo CD for deploys, status page on Statuspage}"
  deploy_and_rollback: "${deploy:Argo CD sync from main, roughly 10 deploys a week, feature flags in LaunchDarkly}"
  escalation_contacts: "${contacts:primary on-call (payments team), secondary on-call, payments team lead, database on-call from platform team, payment provider support line}"
  comms_channels: "${comms:#inc-checkout Slack channel, customer support lead, public status page}"
  business_hours_and_timezone: "${timezone:Europe/Berlin, 24x7 on-call, weekly rotation}"
  known_gaps: "${gaps:no alert on certificate expiry yet, replica lag is not graphed}"

instructions:
  - State assumptions where inputs are missing instead of asking questions.
  - Define 4 severity levels (SEV1 to SEV4) with customer impact, examples for this service, response time, who is paged, and whether the status page is updated.
  - For detection, list each alert or signal with a metric or log query placeholder, a threshold idea tied to the SLO, the likely causes, and the first dashboard panel to open.
  - Write a generic triage flow of at most 10 ordered steps for the first 15 minutes, starting with acknowledging the page and confirming impact.
  - Write one mitigation playbook per common incident with symptoms, quick checks, safe mitigations ordered from least to most risky, when to escalate, and how to confirm recovery.
  - Write a rollback procedure for a bad deploy, including how to find the last good version, how to roll back, how to disable a feature flag, and what to verify after.
  - Provide short communication templates for the incident channel kickoff, a 30-minute update, the status page (investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved), and a note to customer support.
  - Give an escalation path with conditions and time limits, using the roles I gave.
  - Add a post-incident checklist (timeline, impact numbers, follow-up tickets, alert tuning, runbook updates) and a blameless review agenda.
  - Turn known gaps into follow-up tasks with an owner role.
  - Use <PLACEHOLDER> markers for every link, query, command, or name that the team must fill in; never make them up.

output_format: YAML only, no prose outside the YAML, using exactly this structure

output_schema:

  service:
    name: string
    purpose: string
    dependencies: [string]
    slo: string
    owners: string
  severity_levels:
    - level: SEV1 | SEV2 | SEV3 | SEV4
      customer_impact: string
      examples: [string]
      response_time: string
      page: [string]
      status_page_update: boolean
  detection_signals:
    - name: string
      signal: string
      query_placeholder: string
      threshold_idea: string
      likely_causes: [string]
      first_panel_to_open: string
  triage_steps:
    - step: number
      action: string
      look_at: string
      decision: string
  playbooks:
    - incident: string
      symptoms: [string]
      quick_checks: [string]
      mitigations:
        - order: number
          action: string
          risk: low | medium | high
          command_placeholder: string
      escalate_when: string
      confirm_recovery: [string]
  rollback:
    find_last_good_version: [string]
    steps: [string]
    feature_flag_kill_switch: [string]
    verify_after: [string]
  comms_templates:
    incident_channel_kickoff: string

  post_incident_checklist: [string]

  follow_up_tasks:
    - task: string

kayitlar.aciklama: Viktorya tarzı cam serayı tasarım konseptine ve hazır görsel prompt'larına dönüştürür.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Turns a Victorian glass conservatory idea into a design concept and ready image prompts.
kayitlar.metin:
Act as a conservatory and glasshouse designer and as a visualization art director. I will describe the Victorian-style glass conservatory I am imagining. You will turn it into a tight concept: the building, its iron and glass structure, the plants, the furniture, the floor and water features, the light and mood, with a numbered list of fixed design details plus two ready-to-use image prompts that show the SAME building from two viewpoints at two times of day, so the two AI images look like photos of one real place.

Era and inspiration: ${era:High Victorian, around 1870, inspired by public palm houses but at the scale of a private estate}
Purpose and scale: ${purpose:a private winter garden attached to nothing, standing alone at the end of a formal garden, about 14 m long, 8 m wide, 7 m high}
Structure and materials I like: ${structure:white-painted wrought iron, arched ribs, a diamond lattice glass roof, a low pale stone plinth wall}
Plants: ${plants:hanging Boston ferns, kentia palms in terracotta pots, tree ferns, orchids on a side shelf, moss}
Furniture and features: ${features:ornate cast-iron benches, a small round mosaic fountain with koi in the center, brass pendant lanterns}
Floor: ${floor:black-and-white checkerboard marble}
Mood: ${mood:calm, humid, timeless, a little romantic, a place to read on a Sunday morning}
Outside the building: ${outside:a gravel path between low box hedges, climbing pink roses on the front, a formal English garden}
View A: ${view_a:interior at eye level from just inside the front doors, looking down the central aisle, early morning sun with misty light shafts}
View B: ${view_b:exterior from the gravel garden path facing the front entrance at blue hour, warm lamps glowing inside}

Please produce:

1. Concept
   - A name idea for the conservatory (for my use only, it will not appear in the images) and a two-sentence story of how it should feel to step inside.
   - Architecture: footprint, height, roof form, rib spacing, glazing pattern, ridge details, entrance, ventilation features, and how the iron is finished, described in plain construction terms.
   - Interior layout: the central aisle, where the fountain sits, where benches, palms, ferns, and shelves go, and where the lanterns hang, described from the entrance looking in.
   - Planting plan: each plant group with its position and the effect it creates (height, texture, light filtering).
   - Palette: 6 named colors (simple names like "chalk white" or "fern green") and where each one appears.
   - Materials and finishes: iron, glass (clear, slightly wavy old glass, condensation), stone, marble, mosaic, brass, terracotta, and wood.

2. Fixed design details (the consistency list)
   A numbered list of 14 to 18 details that must look identical in every image: footprint and proportions, roof shape, rib count and spacing, the glazing pattern, the ridge cresting and finials, the plinth wall, the entrance doors and fanlight, the floor pattern, the fountain, the benches, the lanterns, the palms, the ferns, and anything visible from both inside and outside, each with its exact position. Write each one as a short, concrete phrase an image generator can follow (for example "a round fountain basin about 2 m across, clad in deep blue and gold mosaic, at the exact center of the hall").

3. Image prompt A: the base view
   One detailed prompt for an AI image generator: photoreal architectural interior photography from the view A position, in view A light. Include every fixed detail visible from there in its correct position (left and right as seen from the camera), camera height and lens, light direction, atmosphere (mist, humidity, light shafts), mood, and a 16:9 landscape composition. End with exclusions (no people, no readable text, no signage, no modern objects).

4. Image prompt B: the second view
   One detailed prompt for view B, written for a text-only image generator that cannot see image A: restate ALL fixed details again in full words (never "same as before"), place each one correctly for the new camera position, describe what is newly visible from outside (the front gable, the plinth, the ridge cresting, the path, the roses), describe which interior details can be seen through the glass and the open doors, and change only the viewpoint, time of day, and lighting. Keep the structure, colors, and proportions identical.

5. Consistency checklist
   Ten yes/no checks to compare image B against image A (for example "Is the roof glazing still a diamond lattice between the white arched ribs?").

6. Practical notes
   A short list on real-world feasibility: heating and humidity for these plants, ventilation, shading in summer, maintenance of painted iron and old glass, safety glass options, and a rough order of magnitude for building or restoring something similar, labeled as an estimate.

Rules:
- Keep the design historically believable for the stated era; flag anything that would be anachronistic or structurally unrealistic.
- Use plain color names and concrete shapes; avoid vague words like "beautiful" or "magical" on their own.
- No readable text, plaques, signs, or numbers anywhere in the image prompts.
- No real named buildings, brand names, or real people in the image prompts.
- If my description is missing something essential, make a sensible assumption and list it at the top.

kayitlar.ad: Paper Quilling Portrait of a Hummingbird and Hibiscus
kayitlar.aciklama: Sinekkuşu ve hibiskusu gösteren kâğıt quilling sanat eseri fotoğrafı üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a photo of a paper quilling artwork of a hummingbird and hibiscus.
kayitlar.metin: A close, slightly elevated studio photograph of a finished paper quilling artwork lying flat on a pale wooden craft table, 16:9 landscape composition, the artwork filling most of the frame. The piece shows a ruby-throated hummingbird in mid-hover on the left, its long thin beak dipping into a large open magenta hibiscus flower on the right. Everything is built from thousands of narrow paper strips, about 3 mm wide, rolled into tight coils, teardrops, marquise shapes, and open scrolls, glued on edge so the paper stands up from a soft cream cotton-paper background. The hummingbird's back and crown are tight coils in emerald and metallic-sheen green, its throat a patch of tiny ruby-red teardrop coils, its belly pale grey and white loose coils, its wings two fans of long fine strips in smoky grey-blue graded from dark at the base to light at the tips, suggesting motion; a small black coil for the eye with a single white dot. The hibiscus has five broad petals made of rows of magenta and hot pink strips shaped in waves, a deep crimson center, and a long yellow stamen column tipped with tiny orange coils; two glossy green leaves made of veined leaf-green strips, a curling stem, and one closed bud. A few loose spiral tendrils and three small lavender filigree flowers fill the background space. Real craft details: visible paper edges and layers, slight variations in coil tightness, tiny glue sheen at a few joints, and soft shadows cast by the raised strips onto the cream base. At the edge of the frame, out of focus: a slotted quilling tool, a small bundle of colored strips, and a pair of fine tweezers. Soft diffused window light from the upper left, gentle contact shadows, shallow depth of field with the hummingbird's head and the flower center sharpest, the far corners softly blurred. Photoreal product photography of handmade paper art, true colors, calm and delicate mood. Not a drawing or a painting of quilling: a real photographed paper object. No text, no letters, no signature, no watermark, no hands.
kayitlar.description: Sinekkuşu ve hibiskusu gösteren kâğıt quilling sanat eseri fotoğrafı üretir.

kayitlar.ad: Noir Comic Panel of a Detective in a Rain-Soaked Phone Booth
kayitlar.aciklama: Yağmurlu gecede telefon kulübesindeki dedektifi gösteren siyah-beyaz noir çizgi roman karesi çizer.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Creates a black-and-white noir comic panel of a detective in a rain-soaked phone booth.
kayitlar.metin: A single black-and-white noir comic book panel, 16:9 landscape, framed by a thin solid black panel border with a narrow white gutter around it. Night on an empty city street in heavy rain. Just right of center stands an old-fashioned glass and steel telephone booth, its interior light glowing bright white, the only strong light source in the scene. Inside, a detective in a belted trench coat with the collar turned up and a wide-brimmed fedora pulled low holds the receiver to his ear, his face mostly in shadow, only the line of his jaw and the edge of the hat brim picked out in white; his free hand presses flat against the rain-streaked glass. Water runs down the booth's panes in drawn streaks. Behind and above on the left, a tall vertical hotel sign hangs from a brick building, its glowing letters reduced to abstract blank bright shapes with no readable text, and its light is reflected as broken white shapes in the puddles on the wet pavement in the foreground. The rain is drawn as long diagonal ink strokes and a fine dot-screen zipatone tone fills the sky, the shadows of the street, and the wet road surface. Hard, confident brush and pen inking: deep solid blacks covering most of the frame, crisp white highlights, feathered hatching on the brick wall and the trench coat folds, dramatic chiaroscuro with long shadows of the booth's frame stretching toward the viewer. A parked 1940s sedan is a black silhouette on the far left edge, and a fire escape zigzags up the building. Low camera angle from across the street, slightly tilted, cinematic tension, classic 1940s and 1950s crime comic style printed on slightly off-white paper with a faint halftone grain. Strictly black, white, and grey tones only. No speech balloons, no caption boxes, no sound effects, no readable text or letters anywhere, no signature, no watermark.
kayitlar.description: Yağmurlu gecede telefon kulübesindeki dedektifi gösteren siyah-beyaz noir çizgi roman karesi çizer.

kayitlar.ad: Cut-Paper Shadow Box of a Coral Reef Aquarium
kayitlar.aciklama: Mercan resifi akvaryumunu katmanlı kesme kâğıtla gösteren gölge kutusu fotoğrafı üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a photo of a layered cut-paper shadow box depicting a coral reef aquarium.
kayitlar.metin: A museum-quality photograph of a deep wooden shadow box hanging on a pale grey gallery wall, seen straight on at eye level, 16:9 landscape composition with the box filling most of the frame. Inside the box is a layered cut-paper diorama of a coral reef aquarium, made of about twelve hand-cut paper layers spaced a few millimeters apart so each layer casts a soft shadow on the one behind it. The back layers are smooth gradients of turquoise and deep teal paper suggesting open water, with faint wavy cut-outs of light rays; middle layers hold silhouettes of distant coral in muted blue-green; the front layers are rich and colorful: branching coral in coral pink and salmon, a round brain coral in ochre with a carved maze pattern, a fan coral in violet with delicate lace-like cut holes, swaying sea grass in two greens, and a bright magenta anemone with fringed tentacles cut in fine strips. A single small yellow fish with a thin black stripe and a tiny punched eye swims near the anemone, slightly raised on its own layer. Columns of small circular bubbles, punched from white and pale aqua paper, rise on the right. A sandy floor of textured cream paper with a few tiny cut shells runs along the bottom. The box frame is natural oak, about 8 cm deep, with a clean inner white mat and a sheet of museum glass showing only a faint reflection at one corner. Soft directional light from the left side lights up the paper edges and creates crisp, layered shadows inside the box, emphasizing depth; the paper fibers, cut edges, and slight curl of thin pieces are visible. Calm, wondrous mood, true colors, craft and fine-art photography, sharp focus across the whole diorama. No text, no letters, no labels, no signature, no watermark, no people.
kayitlar.description: Mercan resifi akvaryumunu katmanlı kesme kâğıtla gösteren gölge kutusu fotoğrafı üretir.

kayitlar.ad: Victorian Glass Conservatory Interior with Ferns (Morning Light)
kayitlar.aciklama: Sabah ışığında eğrelti otlarıyla dolu Viktorya tarzı cam sera iç mekânını gösteren görsel üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a morning-light interior image of a Victorian glass conservatory full of ferns.
kayitlar.metin: Photoreal architectural interior photograph of a High Victorian glass conservatory in early morning, taken from standing eye level (1.6 m) just inside the open front double doors, looking straight down the central aisle along the length of the hall, 24mm lens, 16:9 landscape composition, symmetrical one-point perspective. Fixed design details: a rectangular hall about 14 m long, 8 m wide, and 7 m high at the ridge; a low pale cream limestone plinth wall about 70 cm high runs around the base, with tall clear glass walls in white-framed rectangular panes above it, and a curved barrel-vault glass roof springing from the tops of the walls. Nine slender white-painted wrought iron arched ribs, about 1.5 m apart, cross the hall from wall to wall, each with small white scroll brackets where the wall meets the roof. Between the ribs the roof is glazed in a diamond lattice of thin white glazing bars, the old glass slightly wavy and misted with condensation. The far end wall is a glazed semicircular gable following the vault curve, with a tall tree fern on each side of it. The floor is black and white marble checkerboard in large square tiles, laid square to the 2 m wide central aisle, polished and a little damp. At the exact center of the hall sits a round fountain basin about 2 m across with a low rim clad in deep blue and gold mosaic, a small three-tier white stone bowl spout trickling water, and orange and white koi visible in the water. Two ornate black cast-iron benches with fern-pattern backs and pale oak seat slats stand one on each side of the aisle, facing the fountain. Four tall kentia palms in large terracotta pots line the aisle, two on each side between the camera and the fountain. Lush Boston ferns in round wire baskets hang on thin chains from every rib along both sides of the aisle. A row of five brass pendant lanterns with frosted glass globes hangs on long chains above the central aisle, switched off. Along the right wall runs a slatted oak plant shelf with white orchids and small terracotta pots; low beds of moss and ground ferns line the plinth on both sides. Light and atmosphere: low morning sun from the left streams through the glass walls in long, clearly visible golden light shafts cutting through soft humid mist, dappled diamond-pattern shadows from the roof fall across the checkerboard floor, droplets of condensation catch the light, fresh green and chalk-white palette with warm gold highlights. Calm, quiet, timeless mood, crisp architectural detail, true colors, no distortion of vertical lines. No people, no readable text, no signs or plaques, no modern objects, no watermark.
kayitlar.description: Sabah ışığında eğrelti otlarıyla dolu Viktorya tarzı cam sera iç mekânını gösteren görsel üretir.
