kayitlar.aciklama: GraphQL şema tasarımı, tip üretimi ve null kullanımı gibi API tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Defines GraphQL API preferences like schema design, type generation and nullability.
kayitlar.metin:
# GraphQL API taste of a platform engineer
- Design the schema around client use cases and domain language, not around database tables. Confidence: 0.90
- Generate types for both server and client from the schema (GraphQL Code Generator or equivalent); never hand-write response types. Confidence: 0.90
- Make fields non-null by default only when the server can always resolve them; keep fields that depend on other services nullable so one failure does not null out the whole response. Confidence: 0.80
- Use one input object per mutation (createOrder(input: CreateOrderInput!)) and return a payload type, not the bare entity. Confidence: 0.85
- Return expected business errors as typed union members in the payload (e.g. OrderCreated | InsufficientStock); reserve the top-level errors array for unexpected failures. Confidence: 0.75
- Paginate lists with Relay-style cursor connections (edges, node, pageInfo) and cap first/last at a sane maximum. Confidence: 0.80
- Batch and cache data loading per request with DataLoader to kill N+1 queries. Confidence: 0.95
- Enforce query depth and complexity limits at the gateway. Confidence: 0.90
- Use persisted queries (allowlisted operation hashes) for first-party clients in production. Confidence: 0.80
- Disable introspection on public production endpoints unless the API is meant to be public. Confidence: 0.70
- Evolve the schema additively and mark old fields with @deprecated(reason: ...); never version the endpoint with /v2. Confidence: 0.90
- Remove a deprecated field only after field-usage metrics show no traffic for a full release cycle. Confidence: 0.85
- Run schema diff checks in CI and fail the build on breaking changes. Confidence: 0.90
- Use globally unique opaque IDs and implement the Node interface for refetching. Confidence: 0.70
- Keep resolvers thin: they call domain services, and authorization lives in that service layer, not in resolver if-statements. Confidence: 0.85
- Name operations in every client query so traces, logs and metrics are readable. Confidence: 0.90
- Colocate fragments with the UI components that use them. Confidence: 0.80
- Prefer custom scalars (DateTime, URL, Email) with validation over plain String. Confidence: 0.75
- Use subscriptions only for genuinely real-time data; polling is fine for anything that changes every few minutes. Confidence: 0.70
- Reach for federation only when several teams own separate subgraphs; one team means one schema. Confidence: 0.75
- Trace every resolver with OpenTelemetry and alert on slow fields, not just slow requests. Confidence: 0.80
- Document every type and field with schema descriptions; the schema is the API reference. Confidence: 0.85
kayitlar.description: GraphQL şema tasarımı, tip üretimi ve null kullanımı gibi API tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.

kayitlar.aciklama: Redis'te cache-aside, TTL ve önbellek tutarlılığı gibi önbellekleme tercihlerini tanımlar.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Defines Redis caching preferences like cache-aside, TTLs and cache consistency.
kayitlar.metin:
# Redis Caching taste of a backend engineer
- Default to cache-aside: read from Redis, fall back to the source of truth on a miss, then populate the cache. Confidence: 0.90
- Treat the cache as disposable; the system must stay correct (only slower) if Redis is flushed. Confidence: 0.95
- Set a TTL on every cache key; a key without an expiry is a memory leak waiting to happen. Confidence: 0.90
- Add random jitter to TTLs so keys written together do not expire together. Confidence: 0.85
- Namespace keys as service:entity:id:version (e.g. catalog:product:42:v3) and bump the version on breaking format changes. Confidence: 0.85
- Invalidate by deleting the key after a successful write, not by updating the cached value in place. Confidence: 0.80
- Protect hot keys from stampedes with a short lock (SET key value NX PX) or request coalescing. Confidence: 0.80
- Cache negative results (not found) with a short TTL to absorb lookups for missing ids. Confidence: 0.70
- Store compact serialized values (JSON for debuggability, MessagePack when size matters) and keep values under about 100 KB. Confidence: 0.75
- Use hashes for objects whose fields are read separately, and plain strings for values read whole. Confidence: 0.70
- Never run KEYS in production; use SCAN with a cursor. Confidence: 0.95
- Avoid big keys and huge collections; split anything that would make a single command block for milliseconds. Confidence: 0.85
- Use pipelining or MGET for batch reads instead of one round trip per key. Confidence: 0.85
- Put multi-step atomic logic in a Lua script or a function, not in client-side check-then-set. Confidence: 0.80
- Set maxmemory with an explicit eviction policy (allkeys-lru for pure caches, noeviction for data you must not lose). Confidence: 0.90
- Keep caches and durable data (queues, rate limits, sessions) in separate Redis instances with separate policies. Confidence: 0.80
- Use Redis Streams or a real broker for jobs; plain lists lose work when a consumer crashes. Confidence: 0.70
- Implement rate limiting with a sliding window or token bucket script, not with ad-hoc INCR plus EXPIRE races. Confidence: 0.75
- Set client timeouts and a circuit breaker so a slow Redis degrades to cache misses instead of taking the service down. Confidence: 0.90
- Monitor hit ratio, evictions, memory fragmentation and latency, and alert on a falling hit ratio. Confidence: 0.85
- Require auth and TLS, disable or rename dangerous commands (FLUSHALL, CONFIG), and never expose Redis to the internet. Confidence: 0.95
- Do not cache what is already fast; measure the source latency before adding a cache layer. Confidence: 0.80
kayitlar.description: Redis'te cache-aside, TTL ve önbellek tutarlılığı gibi önbellekleme tercihlerini tanımlar.

kayitlar.aciklama: Semantik HTML ve ARIA kullanımı gibi web erişilebilirliği tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Defines web accessibility preferences like semantic HTML and correct ARIA usage.
kayitlar.metin:
# Web Accessibility taste of a frontend engineer
- Use semantic HTML first (button, a, nav, main, label); add ARIA only when no native element fits. Confidence: 0.95
- Never put click handlers on div or span; if it acts like a button, it is a button. Confidence: 0.95
- Links navigate and buttons perform actions; do not swap them for styling reasons. Confidence: 0.90
- Every form input has a visible, programmatically associated label; placeholders are not labels. Confidence: 0.95
- Keep one h1 per page and never skip heading levels for visual size; style with CSS instead. Confidence: 0.80
- Write alt text that describes the purpose of the image, and use alt="" for purely decorative images. Confidence: 0.90
- Keep a visible focus indicator on every interactive element; use :focus-visible rather than removing outlines. Confidence: 0.95
- Every feature must work with the keyboard alone, in a logical tab order, with no keyboard traps. Confidence: 0.95
- Avoid positive tabindex values; fix the DOM order instead. Confidence: 0.90
- Meet WCAG AA contrast: 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text and UI components. Confidence: 0.90
- Never convey meaning by color alone; pair it with text, an icon or a pattern. Confidence: 0.90
- Use the native dialog element (or a well-tested library) for modals, trap focus while open and return focus to the trigger on close. Confidence: 0.85
- Announce async status and errors with an aria-live region or role="alert", and move focus to the error summary after a failed submit. Confidence: 0.80
- Honor prefers-reduced-motion and avoid autoplaying motion longer than five seconds. Confidence: 0.85
- Make touch targets at least 24x24 CSS pixels, ideally 44x44. Confidence: 0.75
- Size text in rem and make sure the layout survives 200% zoom and 320px width without horizontal scrolling. Confidence: 0.85
- Add a "Skip to main content" link as the first focusable element. Confidence: 0.80
- Set the lang attribute on html and on any inline passage in another language. Confidence: 0.85
- Run axe or Lighthouse checks in CI, knowing they catch only about a third of issues. Confidence: 0.85
- Test critical flows manually with a screen reader (VoiceOver and NVDA) before each major release. Confidence: 0.80
- Lint JSX with eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y and treat its errors as build failures. Confidence: 0.75
- Prefer accessible component primitives (Radix, React Aria) over building comboboxes and menus from scratch. Confidence: 0.80
kayitlar.description: Semantik HTML ve ARIA kullanımı gibi web erişilebilirliği tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.

kayitlar.ad: Rental Apartment Viewing Scorecard and Comparison (JSON)
kayitlar.aciklama: Kiralık daire gezilerinden önceliklere göre ağırlıklı puan kartı, uyarılar ve açık sorular çıkarır.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Turns rental apartment viewing notes into weighted scorecards, red flags and open questions.
kayitlar.metin:
{
  "role": "Practical home-search advisor who helps renters judge apartment viewings with clear, evidence-based scores",
  "task": "Turn my notes and photo descriptions from one or more rental apartment viewings into a single strict JSON scorecard package: weighted scores per apartment based on my priorities, red flags, questions still open for the landlord or agent, true monthly cost estimates, a side-by-side comparison, and a clear next step. Never invent facts about a flat I did not mention.",
  "context": {
    "search_area_and_budget": "${budget:city center or close by, max 1,400 per month including bills}",
    "household": "${household:two adults, one works from home, a small dog}",
    "priorities_with_weights": "${priorities:commute 25, natural light and quiet 20, total monthly cost 20, condition and damp 15, kitchen and storage 10, outdoor space 10}",
    "deal_breakers": "${dealbreakers:no pets allowed, visible mold, no washing machine space}",
    "viewing_notes": "${notes:paste notes per apartment: address or nickname, rent, deposit, bills included, size, floor, lift, heating type, windows, noise, damp signs, appliances, landlord comments, photos you took}",
    "commute_targets": "${commute:office near the central station, three days a week}"
  },
  "ask_first": [
    "Rent, deposit, and which bills are included for any apartment where they are missing",
    "Lease length, notice period, and move-in date for each apartment",
    "Pet, smoking, and subletting rules if a deal breaker depends on them",
    "Heating type and any energy rating or typical bill figures the agent gave",
    "Whether the weights should be changed before scoring"
  ],
  "rules": [
    "Use only what I wrote. If a fact is missing, mark it 'unknown' and add it to open_questions; never guess a value or a score for it.",
    "Score each criterion from 1 to 5 with a one-line reason quoting my notes, then compute the weighted total out of 100 using my weights. Show the maths in score_breakdown.",
    "Any deal breaker that is confirmed sets 'eliminated': true with the reason; an unconfirmed one becomes a high-priority open question, not an elimination.",
    "Flag red flags explicitly (damp or mold signs, condensation on windows, musty smell, cracked seals, very old boiler, missing smoke alarm, pressure to pay a deposit before signing, cash-only requests, refusal to show the contract, agent cannot name the owner) with severity and what to check.",
    "Estimate true monthly cost as rent plus likely bills plus commute, marking each estimate as 'given' or 'estimate' with a range.",
    "Treat scam warnings seriously: never recommend paying any money before seeing the contract and verifying the landlord or agent.",
    "This is decision support, not legal advice; suggest checking the lease and local tenant rules before signing.",
    "Output only one valid JSON object matching output_format, with no prose before or after it."
  ],
  "output_format": {
    "assumptions": ["string"],
    "weights_used": [{"criterion": "string", "weight": "number"}],
    "apartments": [
      {
        "name": "string",
        "facts": {"rent": "string", "deposit": "string", "bills_included": ["string"], "size": "string", "floor_and_lift": "string", "heating": "string", "lease_terms": "string"},
        "eliminated": "boolean",
        "elimination_reason": "string | null",
        "score_breakdown": [{"criterion": "string", "score_1_to_5": "number | null", "reason": "string", "weighted_points": "number"}],
        "weighted_total_out_of_100": "number",
        "true_monthly_cost": {"rent": "string", "bills": "string", "commute": "string", "total_range": "string", "basis": "given | estimate | mixed"},
        "strengths": ["string"],
        "red_flags": [{"issue": "string", "severity": "high | medium | low", "what_to_check": "string"}],
        "open_questions": [{"question": "string", "ask_who": "landlord | agent | building manager | neighbor", "priority": "high | medium | low"}]
      }
    ],
    "comparison_table": [{"criterion": "string", "values": [{"apartment": "string", "value": "string", "score": "number | null"}]}],
    "ranking": [{"rank": "number", "apartment": "string", "weighted_total": "number", "one_line_why": "string"}],
    "second_viewing_checklist": ["string"],
    "recommendation": {"choice": "string", "confidence": "high | medium | low", "conditions_before_signing": ["string"], "next_step": "string"},
    "disclaimer": "string"
  }
}

kayitlar.ad: New Hire First Week Onboarding Plan Builder (YAML)
kayitlar.aciklama: Yeni çalışan için gün gün program ve hedefler içeren ilk hafta oryantasyon planı hazırlar.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Builds a day-by-day first-week onboarding plan for a new hire.
kayitlar.metin:
role: Thoughtful people manager and onboarding designer for small and mid-sized teams
task: >
  Turn my notes about a new team member, their role, and my team into a complete first week
  onboarding plan as YAML: preparation before day one, a day-by-day schedule, people to meet,
  access and equipment, learning goals, a small first contribution, check-ins, and a simple
  way to collect feedback, so the new hire feels welcome and productive without being overloaded.

inputs:
  new_hire_role: ${role:junior customer support specialist}
  start_date_and_hours: ${start:Monday 09:00, full time, Monday to Friday}
  work_setup: ${setup:hybrid, office on Monday and Wednesday, remote the rest of the week}
  team: ${team:six people in support, one team lead, works closely with the product team}
  manager_availability: ${availability:I am in meetings most afternoons, mornings are free}
  tools_and_systems: ${tools:helpdesk tool, team chat, shared docs, internal knowledge base}
  first_contribution_idea: ${contribution:answer simple tickets with a buddy reviewing replies}
  known_constraints: ${constraints:laptop delivery can take two days, one teammate on holiday}

ask_first:
  - Who can be the onboarding buddy, and how much time they can give each day
  - Which accounts and permissions take the longest to approve, and who approves them
  - The two or three things the new hire must understand by the end of week one
  - Any mandatory trainings (security, privacy, health and safety) and their deadlines
  - The new hire's preferences if known (accessibility needs, preferred name and pronouns, time zone)
  - What a good end of the first month looks like for this role

rules:
  - Spread information across the week; no day should have more than three hours of meetings or trainings.
  - Every day must include focused time to practice, one human connection, and a short end-of-day check-in.
  - Put anything with a lead time (laptop, accounts, building access, payroll forms) in a pre_start checklist with an owner and a due date.
  - Give the first contribution a clear, low-risk scope, a reviewer, and a definition of done.
  - Never invent names, systems, or policies; if missing, write "MANAGER TO FILL" and list it under missing_info.
  - Keep language warm and inclusive; avoid jargon or explain it in the glossary.
  - Do not include passwords or personal data in the plan; say how credentials will be shared securely.
  - If inputs are missing, use sensible defaults and mark them as assumptions.
  - Output only valid YAML matching output_format. No prose outside the YAML.

output_format:
  summary:
    role: string
    start: string
    week_one_goals: [string]
    assumptions: [string]
    missing_info: [string]
  pre_start_checklist:
    - item: string
      owner: string
      due: string
      done: boolean
  welcome_message_draft: string
  days:
    - day: string
      location: string
      theme: string
      schedule:
        - time: string
          activity: string
          with: string
          purpose: string
      focus_time: string
      end_of_day_check_in: [string]
  people_to_meet:
    - name_or_role: string
      why: string
      when: string
      format: string
  access_and_equipment:
    - system: string
      access_level: string
      requested_by: string
      ready_by: string
  learning_plan:
    - topic: string
      resource: string
      time_needed: string
      check_understanding: string
  first_contribution:
    description: string
    reviewer: string
    definition_of_done: [string]
    target_day: string
  buddy_guide:
    daily_time: string
    responsibilities: [string]
  feedback:
    end_of_week_questions: [string]
    manager_reflection: [string]
  glossary:
    - term: string
      meaning: string
  week_two_preview: [string]

kayitlar.ad: Italian Renaissance Fresco of a Harbor Market with Merchant Galleys
kayitlar.aciklama: Ticaret kadırgalarıyla hareketli bir liman pazarını İtalyan Rönesans freski olarak görselleştirir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates an Italian Renaissance fresco of a busy harbor market with merchant galleys.
kayitlar.metin: A wide Italian Renaissance fresco of a busy harbor market on a sunny morning, painted on weathered lime plaster. Two large wooden merchant galleys with loosely hanging ochre sails are moored at a stone quay on the left, with a few smaller boats on the calm turquoise lagoon behind them. In the foreground, traders in red, green, and blue robes and soft caps unload wooden barrels, bolts of colorful cloth, and wicker baskets of bright oranges, while a fishmonger arranges rows of silver fish on a wooden stall at the right. Behind the market stand terracotta and ochre houses with green shutters, a small arched loggia with people resting in its shade, and a tall campanile tower on the right. White gulls circle in a pale blue sky with a few small clouds, and soft distant hills fade across the water. Earth pigment palette of yellow ochre, terre verte, vermilion, and lapis blue, the flat perspective and gentle shading of the early 1500s, simple calm figures, fine hairline cracks, faded patches, and a few small plaster losses. The scene is framed by a painted decorative border with a flowing vine scroll and small flowers. Wide landscape 16:9. No text, no signatures, no modern objects.
kayitlar.description: Ticaret kadırgalarıyla hareketli bir liman pazarını İtalyan Rönesans freski olarak görselleştirir.

kayitlar.ad: Photoreal Macro of Frost Crystals on a Red Maple Leaf at Sunrise
kayitlar.aciklama: Gün doğumunda kırmızı akçaağaç yaprağındaki kırağı kristallerinin makro fotoğrafını üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates a photoreal macro of frost crystals on a red maple leaf at sunrise.
kayitlar.metin: A photoreal macro photograph of delicate frost crystals on a single bright red maple leaf lying flat on dark green moss at sunrise. The leaf fills the center of the frame, its five pointed lobes edged with feathery white ice needles that follow the serrated margins and run along the veins. Tiny hexagonal ice plates and frozen dew beads cover the red surface and sparkle like glass, each bead catching a small point of warm light. Low golden sunlight comes from behind and to the upper right, giving the frost a glowing rim and making the leaf's red look rich and saturated. The moss around the leaf is crusted with fine frost, and the background melts into soft, creamy bokeh of more frosted leaves and grass blades in amber, gold, and cool blue tones. Very shallow depth of field with crisp focus on the crystals in the middle of the leaf, 100mm macro lens look, natural light, high detail and fine texture, calm and quiet late autumn mood. Wide landscape 16:9. No text, no people, no insects.
kayitlar.description: Gün doğumunda kırmızı akçaağaç yaprağındaki kırağı kristallerinin makro fotoğrafını üretir.

kayitlar.ad: Scrimshaw Engraving of a Clipper Ship and a Sea Serpent in a Storm
kayitlar.aciklama: Fırtınada deniz yılanıyla boğuşan klipper gemisini skrimşo gravür tarzında çizer.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Creates a scrimshaw-style engraving of a clipper ship and a sea serpent in a storm.
kayitlar.metin: A wide scrimshaw-style engraving of a three-masted clipper ship under full sail battling towering storm waves, while a long coiled sea serpent rises from the sea beside it on the right. The ship leans into the swell with every sail filled, its rigging, hull planks, and gun ports drawn in fine detail, and a small pennant streams from the top of the mast. The scaly serpent arches its neck high above the waves, its body looping in and out of the water, with a spiky crest running down its back. Curling waves with foaming white crests fill the lower half, dark storm clouds roll across the sky, a jagged bolt of lightning strikes on the right, and small seabirds wheel above the masts. Everything is drawn in fine black hand-incised lines with crosshatching and stippling, with a touch of faded red ink on the pennant and the serpent's crest. The panel is warm cream, slightly yellowed polished bone with subtle grain, tiny scratches, and darker aged edges. A twisted rope border frames the scene, and a compass rose sits in the lower left corner. Antique 19th-century sailor folk art look, high detail. Wide landscape 16:9. No text, no letters, no signatures.
kayitlar.description: Fırtınada deniz yılanıyla boğuşan klipper gemisini skrimşo gravür tarzında çizer.

kayitlar.ad: Steam Locomotive Crossing a Stone Viaduct over an Autumn River Valley
kayitlar.aciklama: Sonbahar nehir vadisi üzerindeki taş viyadükten geçen buharlı lokomotifin görselini üretir.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Generates an image of a steam locomotive crossing a stone viaduct over an autumn valley.
kayitlar.metin: A black steam locomotive pulling four maroon passenger carriages crosses a tall weathered grey stone viaduct over a deep autumn river valley in the soft light of early morning. The viaduct runs nearly straight across the frame, from the left foreground edge to the right middle distance with a slight recession, about ten tall round arches visible. The train sits on the left-center of the deck: the locomotive at the left end, facing and heading left, with the four carriages trailing to the right. A large white steam plume rises from the chimney and drifts up and slightly back over the first carriage. Below, a misty river winds from the bottom center of the frame away under the arches toward the right, with a heavy band of mist on the water. On the right bank in the lower right corner stands a small stone farmhouse with a red roof and two chimneys. Both hillsides are covered with orange, red, gold, and green autumn trees. Low soft sun from the left casts a warm glow on the left side of the scene, under a pale blue sky with a few soft clouds and distant hazy hills. Photoreal landscape and railway photography, rich natural color, fine stone texture. Wide landscape 16:9. No people visible, no text, no signs, no logos.

kayitlar.aciklama_en: Animates the steam train image as the first frame into a calm cinematic short video.
kayitlar.metin: Start from the step 2 image "Steam Locomotive Crossing a Stone Viaduct over an Autumn River Valley" as the exact first frame, and animate it into a calm ${duration:6}-second cinematic shot. Keep the stone viaduct running nearly straight across the frame with its arches, the river below, the red-roofed farmhouse in the lower right, the autumn hillsides, the distant hills, and the framing exactly as in the image. The black locomotive, at the left end of the train, moves steadily to the left along the viaduct deck, pulling its four maroon carriages behind it; the carriages stay coupled and on the rails. Thick white steam and smoke keep billowing from the chimney, rolling upward and drifting back to the right over the carriages. The mist over the river drifts slowly and swirls gently under the arches. Leaves on the nearby trees stir softly in the breeze. Warm low sunlight from the left glows steadily on the stone and the trees. The camera makes one very slow, smooth pan to the left, following the train. Natural, realistic motion, no cuts, no new objects, no people, no text.

kayitlar.aciklama: Küçük PR'lar ve açıklayıcı açıklamalar gibi kod inceleme tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Defines code review preferences like small PRs and clear PR descriptions.
kayitlar.metin:
# Code Review taste of a staff engineer
- Keep pull requests small enough to review in one sitting, ideally under 400 changed lines; split refactors from behavior changes. Confidence: 0.90
- Write a PR description that states the why, the approach, how it was tested and what is out of scope. Confidence: 0.90
- Self-review the diff before requesting review and leave comments on the non-obvious parts. Confidence: 0.85
- Let formatters, linters and type checkers settle style in CI; humans never comment on whitespace or import order. Confidence: 0.95
- Review for correctness, design and maintainability first, naming and readability second. Confidence: 0.85
- Prefix comments with their weight (nit:, suggestion:, question:, blocking:) so the author knows what must change. Confidence: 0.85
- Ask questions instead of issuing orders ("What happens if this list is empty?"). Confidence: 0.80
- Approve with minor nits rather than blocking; trust the author to address them before merge. Confidence: 0.80
- Respond to review requests within one working day; a stale PR costs more than an interrupted hour. Confidence: 0.85
- Require tests for every bug fix that would have failed before the fix. Confidence: 0.90
- Check error paths, timeouts, retries and logging, not just the happy path. Confidence: 0.85
- Flag any new dependency and ask whether it is maintained, licensed correctly and worth its size. Confidence: 0.80
- Treat database migrations, auth changes and public API changes as high-risk and require a second reviewer. Confidence: 0.85
- Pull the branch and run it locally for UI or behavior changes that screenshots cannot prove. Confidence: 0.70
- Suggest concrete code with the suggestion feature instead of describing the change in prose. Confidence: 0.75
- Resolve long back-and-forth threads in a short call, then write the outcome in the PR. Confidence: 0.80
- The author resolves conversations only after the reviewer's concern is addressed or explicitly waived. Confidence: 0.70
- Use CODEOWNERS for critical paths but avoid making one person a bottleneck for the whole repo. Confidence: 0.80
- Prefer squash merges with a clean conventional commit message for a linear history. Confidence: 0.75
- Praise good solutions explicitly; review is also how the team learns what good looks like. Confidence: 0.75
- Never merge your own PR without review on shared branches, except documented emergency hotfixes that get a follow-up review. Confidence: 0.85
kayitlar.description: Küçük PR'lar ve açıklayıcı açıklamalar gibi kod inceleme tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.

kayitlar.aciklama: Olay adlandırma ve komut-olay ayrımı gibi olay güdümlü mimari tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Defines event-driven architecture preferences like event naming and commands vs events.
kayitlar.metin:
# Event-Driven Architecture taste of a distributed systems engineer
- Use events to announce facts that already happened (OrderPlaced), and commands only for requests to a single owner (ChargeCard). Confidence: 0.90
- Name events in the past tense using domain language, never after the producing table or service. Confidence: 0.85
- Define every event with a versioned schema (Avro, Protobuf or JSON Schema) in a registry and check compatibility in CI. Confidence: 0.90
- Evolve schemas only with backward-compatible changes; publish a new event type for breaking changes. Confidence: 0.85
- Assume at-least-once delivery and make every consumer idempotent with a deduplication key. Confidence: 0.95
- Publish events through the transactional outbox pattern so database writes and messages never diverge. Confidence: 0.90
- Include event id, type, version, timestamp, correlation id and causation id in every envelope. Confidence: 0.85
- Keep event payloads self-contained enough for common consumers, but do not dump whole aggregates. Confidence: 0.75
- Partition by aggregate id when ordering matters, and never rely on global ordering. Confidence: 0.85
- Route poison messages to a dead-letter queue after bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Confidence: 0.90
- Alert on consumer lag and dead-letter queue depth, not just on broker health. Confidence: 0.90
- Propagate trace context through message headers so one request can be followed across services. Confidence: 0.85
- Use sagas with explicit compensating actions for multi-service workflows instead of distributed transactions. Confidence: 0.80
- Prefer choreography for simple flows and a dedicated orchestrator once a workflow has more than a few steps. Confidence: 0.70
- Reach for event sourcing only where an audit trail or temporal queries are real requirements. Confidence: 0.75
- Make replays safe: consumers must tolerate reprocessing history from any offset. Confidence: 0.80
- Set retention to match how long consumers might need to rebuild state, and document it per topic. Confidence: 0.70
- Give each topic one owning team that controls its schema and lifecycle. Confidence: 0.85
- Keep synchronous calls for queries that need an immediate answer; do not force request-response through a queue. Confidence: 0.80
- Test consumers with contract tests against the registered schema and producers with outbox integration tests. Confidence: 0.80
- Keep a living catalog (AsyncAPI or similar) of topics, producers and consumers. Confidence: 0.75
kayitlar.description: Olay adlandırma ve komut-olay ayrımı gibi olay güdümlü mimari tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.

kayitlar.aciklama: SwiftUI ile iOS uygulama geliştirmede mimari ve framework tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.
kayitlar.aciklama_en: Defines architecture and framework preferences for building iOS apps with SwiftUI.
kayitlar.metin:
# SwiftUI iOS App taste of a senior iOS developer
- Build new screens in SwiftUI and drop to UIKit only through UIViewRepresentable for gaps. Confidence: 0.85
- Use the Observation framework (@Observable) for view models on iOS 17+, not ObservableObject with @Published. Confidence: 0.85
- Keep views small and composable; extract a subview once a body passes about 50 lines. Confidence: 0.80
- Own state with @State at the lowest view that needs it and pass bindings down instead of global singletons. Confidence: 0.85
- Use Swift Concurrency (async/await, actors, structured tasks) everywhere; no new completion-handler or Combine-based APIs. Confidence: 0.85
- Start async work with the .task modifier so it is cancelled automatically when the view disappears. Confidence: 0.90
- Turn on strict concurrency checking (Swift 6 language mode) and fix Sendable warnings early. Confidence: 0.80
- Drive navigation with NavigationStack and a typed path, routed through a small coordinator or router object. Confidence: 0.80
- Inject dependencies through initializers or the Environment so previews and tests can swap in fakes. Confidence: 0.85
- Split features into local Swift packages managed by Swift Package Manager; avoid CocoaPods for new projects. Confidence: 0.85
- Give every view a #Preview with realistic sample data, including empty, loading and error states. Confidence: 0.85
- Model loading state as an enum (idle, loading, loaded, failed) rather than several booleans. Confidence: 0.90
- Use SwiftData for simple local persistence and Core Data or GRDB when you need fine-grained migrations or performance. Confidence: 0.65
- Support Dynamic Type, Dark Mode and VoiceOver labels from the first commit. Confidence: 0.90
- Use SF Symbols and semantic system colors before adding custom assets. Confidence: 0.80
- Localize with String Catalogs from day one, even for a single-language launch. Confidence: 0.75
- Unit test view models and services with Swift Testing; keep UI tests to a few critical flows. Confidence: 0.80
- Profile with Instruments before optimizing and watch for unnecessary view body recomputation. Confidence: 0.75
- Never block the main thread with networking, decoding or disk I/O. Confidence: 0.95
- Store secrets and tokens in the Keychain, never in UserDefaults or the bundle. Confidence: 0.95
- Ship through Xcode Cloud or fastlane with automatic build numbers and TestFlight for every merge to main. Confidence: 0.75
- Use a structured Logger (os.Logger) with categories instead of print statements. Confidence: 0.85
kayitlar.description: SwiftUI ile iOS uygulama geliştirmede mimari ve framework tercihlerini kural olarak tanımlar.

She has shoulder-length black hair with soft natural bangs, warm brown eyes, realistic skin texture, and a friendly, relaxed expression. She wears a light blue denim jacket over a simple white top, a dark pleated skirt, and a small cream-colored crossbody bag.

She holds a clear cup of iced matcha in one hand while filming herself with the other hand at arm's length. Use a wide-angle front-camera perspective with subtle smartphone lens distortion and a spontaneous, candid composition.

The street is lined with small restaurants and local shops. Pedestrians walk naturally in the background. Warm shop lights and neon signs begin to glow beneath a cool evening sky.

Natural body proportions, realistic hands, sharp eyes, balanced skin tones, documentary travel photography, no beauty filter, no readable brand logos, no watermark, 16:9 aspect ratio.
